page.title: What I can *build* for you
page.intro: Three ways I can help: a complete website or web app, the backend and APIs behind it, and the cloud setup that keeps it running.

seo.title: Services
seo.description: Full-stack web development, backend and API development, and AWS cloud deployment with CI/CD by Mohd Ansar Bux, software engineer in Indore.

items.title: Full-Stack Web Development
items.tagline: A fast, secure website or web app with an admin panel you can update yourself.
items.summary: Company websites and web apps built with Next.js and React, backed by Node.js or Spring Boot, with a CMS for your content.
definition: Full-stack web development means building the whole product: the pages people see, the server and database behind them, and an admin panel so your team can change content without a developer.
I build the front with Next.js and React and the back with Node.js or Spring Boot, then deploy it so it loads fast and is easy to find on Google.

whyNeeded.title: Be found
whyNeeded.description: Most customers search online before they call. A fast, search-friendly site gets you into those searches.

whyNeeded.title: Update it yourself
whyNeeded.description: A built-in CMS lets your team change text, images and pages in minutes, without waiting on a developer.

whyNeeded.title: Look credible
whyNeeded.description: A clean, quick site on your own domain tells clients you're a serious business.

whyNeeded.title: Grow without rebuilding
whyNeeded.description: A modern stack takes on new pages and features as your business grows.

process.title: Discover
process.description: Goals, audience, pages and the content you'll manage.

process.title: Design
process.description: Page layouts and the admin structure, agreed before any code.

process.title: Build
process.description: Frontend, backend, CMS and forms, shared with you as it takes shape.

process.title: Launch & support
process.description: Deployment, domain and SEO setup, then fixes and updates after go-live.

faqs.question: Can I update the website myself?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every site comes with an admin CMS, so you can edit pages, text and images without touching code.

faqs.question: Will it work on phones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every page is responsive and tested on mobile, tablet and desktop.

faqs.question: Do you handle hosting and the domain?
faqs.answer: Yes. I deploy the site, connect your domain and set up SSL, so it's live and secure from day one.

items.title: Backend & API Development
items.tagline: Secure REST APIs with login, roles and permissions, ready to grow with your product.
items.summary: Java/Spring Boot or Node.js backends with JWT authentication, role-based access and documented APIs your frontend team can rely on.
definition: The backend is the part of your product users never see: the server, the database and the APIs your website or app talks to.
I design and build secure REST APIs in Java with Spring Boot or in Node.js with Express, with login, roles and permissions built in from the start.

whyNeeded.title: Secure from day one
whyNeeded.description: JWT authentication, role-based access and CSRF protection keep each piece of data visible only to the right people.

whyNeeded.title: Clear contracts
whyNeeded.description: APIs documented in Postman let your frontend team build without guessing.

whyNeeded.title: Room to grow
whyNeeded.description: A layered architecture keeps the code easy to extend as features and users are added.

process.title: Model
process.description: Map users, roles and data, and agree the API contract.

process.title: Build
process.description: Endpoints, database and security, in small reviewed steps.

process.title: Document & test
process.description: A Postman collection and tests for every endpoint.

process.title: Hand over
process.description: Deployment and a walkthrough, so your team can own it.

idealFor: Frontend teams that need a backend

faqs.question: Spring Boot or Node.js: which should I choose?
faqs.answer: Spring Boot suits large, structured systems with complex business rules; Node.js suits fast-moving products and real-time features. I'll recommend one based on your project and team.

faqs.question: Can you work with my existing frontend team?
faqs.answer: Yes. I agree the API contract with the frontend team up front and document every endpoint in Postman.

faqs.question: How do you handle different user roles?
faqs.answer: With role-based access control: each user gets a role, such as admin or operator, and every endpoint checks it before returning data.

items.title: Cloud Deployment & CI/CD
items.tagline: Your app running on AWS with automatic, repeatable deployments.
items.summary: AWS setup (EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront) with CI/CD pipelines, so every release is quick and predictable.
definition: Cloud deployment puts your application on reliable servers, with the database, file storage, email and monitoring set up properly. I usually use AWS.
CI/CD adds an automatic pipeline: every approved change is built, checked and released the same way, without manual steps.

whyNeeded.title: Faster releases
whyNeeded.description: An automated pipeline makes releases quick and routine. On my current platform it cut deployment time by about 40%.

whyNeeded.title: Fewer mistakes
whyNeeded.description: The same steps run every time, so a release never depends on someone remembering them.

whyNeeded.title: Spot problems early
whyNeeded.description: CloudWatch monitoring and logs show issues before your users report them.

process.title: Review
process.description: Look at your app, traffic and current hosting.

process.title: Set up
process.description: AWS services, domain, SSL and email configured.

process.title: Automate
process.description: A CI/CD pipeline from your Git repository to production.

process.title: Monitor & hand over
process.description: Monitoring, alerts and a short guide for your team.

idealFor: Existing apps moving to the cloud

faqs.question: Do I have to use AWS?
faqs.answer: No. For smaller sites, Vercel or Netlify is often simpler and cheaper. I use AWS when you need more control.

faqs.question: Can you move my existing app?
faqs.answer: Yes. I set up the new environment, move the app and data, and switch the domain over once everything checks out.
